title: Pack your bags!
goals: Talk about planning a trip and explain why you do things with to + verb.
Give opinions with It's + adjective + to + verb (It's easy to find cheap flights).

learn.title: Purpose infinitive: to + verb
learn.html:
To say why you do something, use to + verb in its base form (in Spanish: «para + infinitive»). It answers the question Why…?

QuestionShort answerFull sentence
Why are you going to Puerto Vallarta?To see my cousins.I'm going to Puerto Vallarta to see my cousins.
Why do you go online?To find cheap flights.I go online to find cheap flights.
Why does she need a visa?To travel to Canada.She needs a visa to travel to Canada.
  • Structure: main sentence + to + base verb. The verb after to never changes (no -s, no -ing).
  • For is used with nouns (I went there for a vacation), not with verbs.

watch.wrong: I went to the bank for change money.
watch.right: I went to the bank to change money.
watch.why: «For» + verb is wrong; say to + verb.

watch.wrong: I'm going to Mérida for visit my family.
watch.right: I'm going to Mérida to visit my family.
watch.why: Do not use for before a verb.

watch.wrong: She uses her phone to takes photos.
watch.right: She uses her phone to take photos.
watch.why: After to, the verb is in its base form.

watch.wrong: Why are you studying English? Because to get a better job.
watch.right: Why are you studying English? To get a better job.
watch.why: Answer only with to + verb, without Because.

learn.title: It's + adjective + to + verb (giving opinions)
learn.html:
To give an opinion about an activity, use It's + adjective + to + verb. The subject It is always required.

FormExample
PositiveIt's easy to find a cheap flight online.
NegativeIt's not expensive to fly. / It isn't hard to do.
QuestionIs it easy to find bargains online?
Short answerYes, it is. / No, it isn't.

Useful adjectives: easy, hard, difficult, important, necessary, nice, good, expensive, cheap, safe, boring.

watch.wrong: Is easy to get a visa.
watch.right: It's easy to get a visa.
watch.why: In English, the subject It is required.

watch.right: It's important to take your passport.
watch.why: After the adjective, use to + verb.

watch.wrong: It's very hard for find a hotel in July.

watch.why: Use to, not for, before the verb.

watch.wrong: Is it easy to find cheap flights? Yes, it's.

learn.title: should, need to and could: advice and suggestions
learn.html:
Use these verbs to give advice. Change the strength of the advice.

VerbUseExample
should / shouldn'tnormal advice ("you ought to")You should take a hat. / You shouldn't take high heels.
need tovery important advice ("you have to")You need to have warm clothes.
couldsoft suggestion ("you might")You could borrow your dad's hat.
  • Question: Should I take these shoes? — Yes, you should. / No, you shouldn't.
  • To soften advice: I think you should…, Maybe you should…, You should probably…
  • Should and could go with the base verb, without to and without -s. Need does take to.
  • To say something is not a good idea, use shouldn't; do not use need to or could in the negative to give advice.

watch.why: After should, do not use to.
Should does not change: no -s with he/she/it.

watch.right: You need to take your passport.

watch.wrong: Do I should take this jacket?
watch.why: Should makes questions by itself, without do.

learn.title: Other ways to make suggestions
learn.html:
Besides should and could, there are softer phrases to suggest something to a friend or a roommate.

StructureExample
Why don't you + base verbWhy don't you take a hat?
Do you want to + base verbDo you want to pack some other shoes?
It's a good idea to + base verbIt's a good idea to pack a jacket.
ImperativeTake a flashlight. / Don't forget to pack some batteries.
  • The imperative is used with people you know well, in a friendly tone.
  • To suggest doing something together: Why don't we go sightseeing?

watch.wrong: Why you don't take a map?
watch.right: Why don't you take a map?
watch.why: The order is Why + don't + subject + verb.

watch.wrong: Why don't you to call the airline?
watch.right: Why don't you call the airline?
watch.why: After Why don't you, use the base verb, without to.

watch.wrong: It's good idea to bring a guidebook.
watch.right: It's a good idea to bring a guidebook.

watch.why: The negative imperative is Don't + base verb.

learn.title: Answering suggestions and using I guess
learn.html:
When someone suggests something, you can accept or decline politely.

  • Accept: That's a great idea. / That sounds great. / I'd love to.
  • Hesitate or decline: Maybe. / I don't know. / I guess we could, but… / I'd like to, but…
  • After declining, give an excuse: I'd like to, but I need to keep this job.
  • I guess = I suppose, when you are not sure or want to sound less direct: I guess I need to rest. / Yeah, me too, I guess.

A: We could take a few days off and go backpacking.
B: I don't know. I'd like to, but I need to work.

write.model:
Hi Ana! I'm writing from Mazatlán to tell you about my trip. I came here to relax and to visit my cousin. The weather is great, and the beach is beautiful. It's nice to walk by the sea every morning. It's also fun to try the fresh seafood in the market. Tomorrow I'm going to take a boat to an island to see the birds. I'm going to send you some photos. I hope you are well. See you soon!
Take care,
Luis

One suggestion with could or Why don't you

write.model: Hi Sam! I'm happy you are going to visit my city. You should bring a light jacket, because the evenings are cold. You need to bring comfortable shoes, too, because we are going to walk a lot. You could stay in a hotel near the center, or why don't you stay at my house? It's a good idea to buy your bus ticket early. You don't need to bring much money. You should try the street tacos. They are delicious. See you soon!

reading.title: A weekend in Oaxaca
reading.intro: Read Elena's email and answer the questions.
paragraphs: Hi Laura! I'm writing from Oaxaca. Last month I decided to take a few days off, so I went online to find a cheap bus ticket. It's easy to find bargains if you do some research, and I paid only 450 pesos. I brought a small suitcase, my sunglasses and a guidebook to learn about the city. The bus was comfortable, and the ride only took six hours.

On the first day I went to the market to buy some fruit and to try the famous chocolate. A friendly woman told me, "You should visit Monte Albán early, and you need to take a hat." She was right! The sun is very strong at noon. I also went to a cooking class to learn how to make mole. It isn't hard to make, but it takes a lot of time.

Tomorrow my friend Pablo wants to go hiking in the mountains. I told him, "I'd like to, but I need to rest my feet!" Maybe we could take a short walk instead, and then eat at the restaurant near the hotel. I guess that is a good plan. Why don't you come with us next time? It's a great place to relax. See you soon! Elena

glossary.def: to take a few days away from work or school
something sold for a low price, a good deal
study of a topic to find out facts
not weak; with a lot of power or energy
twelve o'clock in the middle of the day
walking in nature on paths or trails
to stop working or moving to get energy back

listening.title: Getting ready to camp
listening.intro: Listen to the conversation between Mia and Dan. You can repeat it.

lines.text: Hi Dan! Are you ready for the camping trip on Saturday?
Almost. I need to buy a sleeping bag. Do you have an extra one?
No, but you could borrow my brother's. He doesn't use it.
That's a great idea. What else should I bring?
You should take a flashlight and some insect repellent. It's important to protect yourself at night.
Good point. Should I bring a tent?
No, you don't need to. Carlos has a big tent for four people.
Perfect. Why don't we go to the store tonight to buy the food?
I'd like to, but I have to work until nine. Maybe tomorrow morning?
Sure, that sounds great. I guess I can also pack the batteries and a first-aid kit.
Yes, and don't forget to bring sunscreen!
